payload.subject: Mathematics
payload.lesson_type_evidence: We can subtract 47 from 72, but we need to borrow some rupees from our neighbour, who has 10 rupees.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to subtract two-digit numbers using the borrowing method.
Students will explain the process of borrowing from the tens place to the ones place.
learning_outcomes: Given any two-digit subtraction problem requiring borrowing, students will compute the correct difference.
Students will demonstrate borrowing using concrete objects or drawings.
misconceptions: Students may try to subtract the smaller digit from the larger digit in each column without borrowing.
Students may think borrowing changes the overall value of the number incorrectly.
suggested_instructional_sequence: Review place value concepts with tens and ones blocks.
Demonstrate borrowing using physical manipulatives (e.g., base-ten blocks).
Guided practice with step-by-step two-digit subtraction problems.
Independent practice with a variety of subtraction problems.
Apply skills to word problems involving subtraction with borrowing.
